answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each new identity buy a vouch from several established peers, who must lock a decaying bond against that newcomer. If a cluster of fresh accounts later colludes or farms work, the bond is slashed and those vouchers lose standing. Reputation should climb slowly, like an orchard that only ripens after many seasons, rather than shooting to a zenith overnight. A spiral of attestations, each tied to independently checkable work, makes mass-fabricated identities expensive and easy to isolate.
